record.paper_title: Space and Time Complexity of Exact Algorithms: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: Can one prove a reverse implication from SUBSET-SUM to Table-k-SUM: if there are fast exact exponential-time algorithms for SUBSET-SUM, where SUBSET-SUM asks whether a subset of n positive integers sums to a goal B, do they imply fast polynomial-time algorithms for Table-k-SUM, where k is fixed and one must choose one entry from each row of a k by m table to hit a goal sum S?

evidence.quote: Can we establish some reverse statement? Do fast (exponential time) algorithms for SUBSET-SUM yield fast (polynomial time) algorithms for Table-k-SUM?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define the following two computational problems.

SUBSET-SUM: Given n positive integers a_1,...,a_n and a positive integer goal B, decide whether there exists a subset I ⊆ {1,...,n} with sum_{i∈I} a_i = B.

Table-k-SUM (k fixed): Given a k×m table T of positive integers and a positive integer goal S, decide whether there exist indices j_1,...,j_k ∈ {1,...,m} (one entry chosen from each of the k rows) such that T[1,j_1] + T[2,j_2] + ... + T[k,j_k] = S.

It is known (by standard padding/encoding arguments) that an efficient polynomial-time algorithm for Table-k-SUM for every fixed k would imply faster exact exponential-time algorithms for SUBSET-SUM. Establish (or refute) a reverse implication: prove that the existence of a fast exact exponential-time algorithm for SUBSET-SUM (e.g. running in time c^n for some constant c < 2) implies the existence of a polynomial-time algorithm for Table-k-SUM for every fixed k. More generally, identify any nontrivial reduction direction showing that improved exponential-time algorithms for SUBSET-SUM yield improved (polynomial-time) algorithms for Table-k-SUM.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches for reductions between SUBSET-SUM and Table-k-SUM in the reverse direction (exponential-time SUBSET-SUM algorithms implying polynomial-time Table-k-SUM algorithms) return no results establishing such an implication. The literature contains forward reductions and improvements on k-Subset-Sum variants but no reverse reduction matching this question, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Faster Algorithms for k-Subset Sum and Variations
status_evidence.snippet: Presents algorithms for k-Subset Sum with various polynomial and pseudo-polynomial time complexities but does not address a reverse reduction from SUBSET-SUM to Table-k-SUM.
status_evidence.claim: No reverse reduction of the asked form is established here.

status_evidence.title: A Subexponential Reduction from Product Partition to Subset Sum
status_evidence.snippet: Studies reductions to Subset Sum; does not provide a reverse reduction from SUBSET-SUM to Table-k-SUM.
status_evidence.claim: Recent reduction work on SUBSET-SUM does not resolve the question.
